standard_prerequisites.name: Church-Rosser property for the base relation
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The hypothesis of the theorem itself: xredone satisfies CR, invoked at proof lines 656-657 to fill each interior grid cell
standard_prerequisites.use: Guarantees the term R with N_{i-1,j} xredone R and N_{i,j-1} xredone R for every interior cell.

standard_prerequisites.name: Transitive closure as reduction sequences
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The unit's notation: xred is the smallest transitive relation containing xredone (introduced in the statement at source lines 622-626)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reads each grid row and column back as a sequence of xred steps in the final two paragraphs.

core_obligations: Path unwrapping (proof lines 628-633): two xred paths from M, of lengths m and n, written as xredone chains M xredone P_1 xredone ... and M xredone Q_1 xredone ....

Grid construction (lines 634-657): an (m+1) x (n+1) array with the two paths as first row and column, each interior cell a one-step common reduct supplied by the CR hypothesis (lines 644-646 explain the existence of R).
Closing the rectangle (lines 648-651): the bottom row yields P = N_{m,0} xred ... xred N_{m,n} and the right column yields Q xred ... xred N_{m,n}, a common xred reduct.
proof_roadmap: Fix two reduction sequences from the same term.
Grow the rectangle cell by cell using the base CR property.
Read the far corner off the bottom row and right column.
difficulty_reason: The classical scaling lemma (Tait-plotkin style) from parallel to transitive closure (statement 622-626, proof 627-652): explicit rectangular construction with the interior fill justified by the hypothesis. Fully self-contained within the span. H2: standard grid argument, all steps written.
